title: Combination of optokinetic and transcranial brain stimulation (tDCS) in subacute stroke patients with neglect plus EEG
summary:
Neglect after stroke is characterized by impared awareness for stimuli in the contralesional space, and/or reduced use of contralesional limbs (Kerkhoff et al., 2001). Neglect frequently occurs after large, mostly right-hemisphere brain lesions, can have a negative impact on the further course of rehabilitation, and can lead to prolonged hospitalization. The neglect symptomatology is caused by difficulties in directing attention spontaneuosly to the (left) half of space and body. In addition to the structural damage, functional impairments in attention-relevant networks are also assumed to cause neglect symptoms. However, in the early post-stroke phase, the largest reorganization processes (neuroplasticity) occur. This study aims to improve neuroplasticity through the application of plasticity-promoting approaches. For this purpose, a task-specific training, optokinetic stimulation (OKS) is administered simultaneously with electrical brain stimulation over 2x3 days. OKS comprises looking at moving patterns and thereby induce a relatively automatic eye-following movement (visual exploration) even into the neglected visual field. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) aim to rebalance of neuronal activity between the overactivated left (healthy) and underactivated right (damaged) hemispheres of the brain (Sehm et al., 2013, 2012) and to reinforce residual activity in core regions of relevant attentional networks in order to enhance the therapeutic effects of OKS (see also Utz et al., 2010; Zebhauser et al., 2019). For this purpuse, we will conduct a randomized double-blind study in patients with visuospatial neglect and test whether the combined application leads to a stronger reduction of neglect symptomatology compared to OKS only (specifically OKS+sham tdcs as control condition).

In March 2023, an amendment was submitted to the Ethics Committee for consultation. The amendment was approved and accepted on 4/4/2023. Changes concern the inclusion of a resting state EEG before and after the end of training to investigate intervention-related changes on a neurophysiological level, a consent to study participation by the person in charge/caregiver when necessary as well as adjustments of the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Patients with mild neglect will be excluded for this study and a minimum of visual acuity is required for the training.

interventions.name: Experimental group: 2x15 min optocinetic stimulation simultan to bi-hemispheric parietal applied transcranial direct current stimulation 3 times a week for two weeks (in total: 180 min training OKS+tDCS)
Control group: 2x15 min optocinetic stimulation simultan to bi-hemispheric parietal applied sham stimulation 3 times a week for two weeks (in total: 180 min Training OKS+sham tDCS)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Ischemic or hemorrhagic right hemispheric stroke (confirmed by imaging)
•	 Early subacute phase (<= 3 month post stroke) at inclusion
•	Presence of visuospatial neglect (left-sided)
-> patients must meet one of the following criteria (to exclude patients with only very mild neglect symptoms):
a) saccades position test: > 4 errors
b) digital desk test: searching time > 20% slower on the left compared to the  
     right side
c)  mean score in line bisection test: > 2 cm deviation from the center
d) copy task: < 7 points in drawing test
•	sufficient head control and able to sit
•	Sufficient vigilance for study participation
•	 Patient should be able to understand the study - with appropriate explanation - and must be able to provide consent. If necessary, relatives or caregivers can be consulted to assist in the decision-making process or to provide consent for the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
•  Previous stroke
• Extensive posterior infarct with complete hemianopsia
•  Visual disturbances due to ocular muscle palsy
• visual acuity for near vision worse than 30% (measured for better eye or binocular) 
•  Patient with stroke in the brain stem with vestibulo-ocular symptoms 
•  Epilepsy
•  Severe cognitive deficits
•  Severe traumatic brain injury (presen/past), recent head surgery, craniectomy, metal implant in brain
• Pacemaker
•  Psychotropic medications, GABAergic supplements (L-DOPA, SSRI and antiepileptic drugs due to non-epileptic indication are allowed at a constant dose)
•  Pregnancy
•  History of severe alcoholism or substance abuse, severe psychiatric illness such as depression, psychosis (if not in remission)
• participation in other intervention studies
